prompt: Explain inflation using only tailgating metaphors. Do not stop when the metaphors break down.
response:
Inflation is when every car in the parking lot starts creeping closer to your bumper, and suddenly your three-car-lengths of personal space is worth two, then one, then you're practically sniffing the exhaust pipe of the guy in front of you who hasn't even fired up the grill yet.

You came with twelve brats and a dream, but now the guy behind you is riding your ass so hard that your brat purchasing power is shot—used to be one pack per parking spot, now you're lucky to get half a weenie per square foot of asphalt. The lot attendant keeps printing more parking passes but nobody's paved more spaces, so your spot gets subdivided like a timeshare, and now six SUVs think they own the same patch of grass where your cooler used to breathe.

The tailgater behind you? He's not even hungry. He's just following too close because everyone else is following too close, and now the whole lot is a conga line of idling engines and sweating coolers, and the price of ice is whatever the guy in front of you decides it is because his truck bed is basically a central bank with a Yeti full of twenties.

You try to back off, ease up, give yourself some monetary policy room to breathe, but the 49ers fans behind you honk because *their* spot is shrinking too, and their brats are getting cold, and now the whole lot is just cars nose-to-nose like a sausage chain, and the only thing circulating is exhaust and blame.

The grill? The grill is full employment. You thought you were cooking. You're not cooking. You're just compressing meat under the heat of proximity, and the charcoal costs more than the meat now because the charcoal guy saw the tailgating and raised his prices, which is *second-order* tailgating, where the inflation in your spot causes inflation in the spot next to you, which is actually just the same spot now because the lines got repainted by a guy who was tailgating the paint truck.

Your cooler is a savings account. You open it. It's lukewarm Natty and regret. The ice melted into something that isn't even water anymore—it's just future money, diluted, pooling around your last brat like a liquidity trap. You eat the brat. It doesn't matter. You're not hungry either. Nobody's hungry. Everyone's just too close, moving at idle speed, burning gas to go nowhere, and the lot never ends
